messages:
Ana (Support): FYI multiple customers reporting 502/504 gateway errors hitting the hosted inference API since ~08:03 UTC. Primary customer (acct: acme-fabric) says inference requests started failing with 'control-plane dependency error'. Copying logs + repro below.

Ana (Support): Example curl from customer:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
```
Response: 502 Gateway
```json
{"error":"control_plane_error","detail":"configdb: timeout when fetching routing policy (GET /routing/policy)"}
```

Ana (Support): I collected the request IDs: rq_8a1f3c, rq_8a1f7e, rq_8a1fac. All show control-plane 5xx in our logs. Customers also report billing retries — duplicate charges from client retries, so finance flagged one account.

Jordan (Eng Oncall): Thanks Ana. I see a spike in routing-policy svc latency and errors around 08:02–08:10 UTC. Traces show config-db queries taking >5s and timing out. Looks like the control-plane can't read routing rules causing API gateway to return 502. Pushing to eng-platform. @Tony can you check DB connection pool / pgbouncer?

Tony (Infra): On it. Quick dump from pgbouncer at 08:07 UTC:
```
SHOW POOLS;
pool_size=100, active=98, waiting=12
SHOW CLIENTS;
clients=250, avg_wait=1200ms
```
Looks like connection saturation + long-running queries. Also seeing a lot of idle-in-transaction that may be leaking.

Tony (Infra): Running quick health check against configdb cluster (read replica latency): ping 0.02s, p99 query time 4.8s, >10% queries >2s. Might be a runaway analytics job.

Alia (Product): Any idea what triggered the extra load? Was there a release or scheduled job? We had a policy rollout yesterday but it should be light.

DeployBot: deploy/redwood-routing-policy v2.14 rolled at 2026-02-12T07:50:12Z on cluster-a. No immediate errors reported during deploy.

Jordan (Eng Oncall): Correlating traces — many routing-policy requests include large JSON payloads for policy evaluation from an internal job: worker 'policy-backfill' started at 07:58 and iterated policies in a tight loop. That matches the timing. Recommend immediate mitigation: 1) throttle policy-backfill, 2) restart one routing-policy replica to clear stuck connections, 3) temporarily increase DB pool for routing-policy.

Tony (Infra): I can throttle the backfill (scale it to 0.1 rps) and restart routing-policy on cluster-a now. Command I will run: 
```bash
kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deployment/routing-policy --context=cluster-a
# then lower concurrency of policy-backfill via k8s cronjob configmap
```

Ana (Support): I'll let customers know we have an engineering action and will update in 15m. Also created internal incident INC-20260212-34 and attached customer logs. Tagging @Claire for billing follow-up — customers report duplicate charges from retries.

Claire (Billing): Thanks. Please capture the affected account IDs and request IDs. I will prepare credits for impacted customers once we confirm retries >1. Also flag finance to avoid auto-invoice for those tokens.

Jordan (Eng Oncall): Quick repro steps for engineers (from support customer's environment):
1) Send concurrent requests with header X-Redwood-Test=policy to exercise routing.
2) Observe 502/gateway with response body above.
Example: 
```bash
seq 1 50 | xargs -n1 -P10 -I{} curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx' -H 'X-Redwood-Test: policy' -d '{"model":"redwood-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions
```

Jordan (Eng Oncall): Temporary workaround for support to advise customers: add header `X-Redwood-Route: fallback` to bypass routing-policy for critical requests (this hits a conservative routing path and avoids the control-plane call). Use only for short remediation windows.

OpsBot: Incident INC-20260212-34 created and assigned to eng-platform. Priority: P1.

Tony (Infra): Restarted routing-policy deployment on cluster-a at 08:15 UTC. Observed connection pools drop and then warm up. DB p99 improved to 0.4s after killing long-running analytics job.

Jordan (Eng Oncall): I pushed a config change to routing-policy to add rate-limits to the policy-backfill worker and increased pool_size to 150 as an emergency measure. Monitoring shows error rate for control-plane 5xx decreased from 18%->0.5% over 10m.

Ana (Support): Updated customers — most confirmed reduced errors. One account still saw a couple of retries and will need a credit. Sent Claire the list: [acct: acme-fabric, acct: beta-inc].

Claire (Billing): Got the list, starting manual refunds/credits. Will follow up in billing channel with transaction IDs.

Alia (Product): Postmortem items: 1) add circuit-breaker on routing-policy calls from gateway, 2) add backfill job throttling by default, 3) add alert for pgbouncer waiting clients > 50. I'll create a PM ticket.

Jordan (Eng Oncall): Final status: routing-policy healthy, no further 5xx from control-plane in last 20m. Leaving incident open for postmortem. Will attach trace IDs + short timeline to the incident.

Ana (Support): Closing customer-facing loop. Marking thread resolved for now. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
